script_text: Bienvenidos a esta clase sobre Production 52 Accounting Cost en SAP Business One. En esta lección exploraremos las mejores prácticas de consultoría, flujos operativos y configuraciones del sistema. Production and MRP: Production Standard Cost SAP Business One Version 10.0 Welcome to the Production Std. Cost training topic. Although Production Standard Cost fields exist for both perpetual and non perpetual inventory, we only cover the functionality for perpetual inventory in this course. In addition, in order to take this training, you first need to complete the Production Process and By products and Additional Quantity training topics.

After completing this topic, you will be able to: Define a production standard cost for produced items Explain the total production standard cost calculation in the Bill of Materials Describe the production standard cost rollup and update procedures 2 At the end of this topic, you will be able to: Define a production standard cost for produced items Explain the total production standard cost calculation in the Bill of Materials Describe the production standard cost rollup and update procedures Objectives

Business Scenario OC WoodTrend produces custom wooden doors. They use the Production module in SAP Business One to record the production process. There was large fluctuation in the production cost of the doors over the last year and the accountant would like to have better cost prediction. OC WoodTrend decides to manage Production Standard cost in order to analyze and more accurately predict costs. In addition, she would like to set up the relevant cost accounts for the resources in the GL account determination. OC WoodTrend produces custom wooden doors. They use the Production module in SAP Business One to record the production process. There was large fluctuation in the production cost of the doors over the last year and the accountant would like to have better cost prediction. OC WoodTrend decides to manage Production Standard cost in order to analyze and more accurately predict costs. In addition, she would like to set up the relevant cost accounts for the resources in the GL account determination.

Concept Production std. cost is a budgeted production cost which can be compared to the actual production cost. Item Master Data Production Std Cost can be optionally set to the current valuation cost and can also be optionally rolled up through multiple levels of bill of materials. Bill of Materials window displays the Production Std. Cost data for item components, the cost data for resource components and the Production Std Cost data for the produced item. Benefit: Facilitates budget to actual cost comparisons and production variance calculations. Actual Cost Production Std. Cost Difference Copy The main idea behind this feature is to allow us to plan a budget for the production cost. Then we can compare the actual cost of a product to this budgeted cost. In addition we can copy the actual cost of the produced items in a BOM to their Production Std. Cost in an automatic procedure. When working in the Bill of Material and Production Order windows, we can see the Production Std. Cost information. In addition we can analyze the difference between the budgeted cost and the actual cost in the Inventory Audit Trail report.

Resource Std. Cost Definition G L Account Determination (standard) Resource Group Resource Master Data Resource Std. Cost name and Default cost ratio Each resource expense account is related to a resource std. cost The std. cost of a resource is the total of all std. cost elements and is also the actual cost of the resource The cost of a resource is actually the std. cost that is defined in the Resource Master data. This cost is composed from a list of different std. cost elements that are copied from the Resource Group. For the lathe machine, the standard cost is comprised of 3 elements: amortization, maintenance and overhead. Each cost element is related to a certain account in the GL Account Determination window (when using standard G L account determination). There, we can define up to ten resource expense accounts, corresponding to the ten cost components in the Resource Master Data. The cost element in each row in the Resource Master Data is linked by the element number to the cost expense fields in the G L account definition. In OC WoodTrens, Resource Std. Cost 1 of the Lathe machine is named Amortization and refers to account 510160 as shown in the image. The same cost element may have a different name in another resource. In Advanced GL Account Determination it is possible to set rules that connect resource std. cost elements to different G L accounts.

Item Std. Cost Definition Can be entered manually or populated during the Production Std. Cost Rollup procedure The Production Std. Cost of an item is defined manually in the Item Master Data. The Production Std. Cost value can also be copied on a batch basis from the actual product cost of the Item (including component items). This is done in the Rollup procedure. We can see in the image a checkbox indicating this item is included in the Production Std. Cost Rollup. We will explore this option later on in the training.

Production Std. Cost Calculation in the Bill of Materials Production Std. Cost X Qty. Production Std. Cost Planned Avg. Prod. Size + Total Production Std. Cost X Additional Qty In the Bill of Materials we can see the Production Std. Cost that is taken from the Item Master Data as seen in the previous slide. Beneath this field there is another field called: Planned Average Production Size. Here we enter the average quantity of produced items we usually produce in one production run. In our example, we can say that on average, we produce 10 Decorative Wooden Doors every time we go through a production process of Decorative Wooden Doors. This value is relevant for the Additional Quantity we got to know in the By products and Additional Quantity training. The Production Std. Cost of a produced item is equal to the cost of all its components plus the fixed cost of the additional quantity needed to produce one item. In our case, since we need 1 Machine Operator hour, the fixed cost needed to produced 1 Decorative Wooden Doors is 30 divided by a planned average production quantity of 10 multiplied by 1 Additional Quantity. This means that the fixed cost (derived from the Additional Quantity) of producing 1 Decorative Wooden Door is 3. Therefore, the Total Production Std. Cost of the Machine Operator resource is 30, times a quantity of 2 hours, plus 3 of fixed cost. This sums up to 63. At the bottom of the table we see the total production std. cost for the Decorative Wooden Door. Note that this calculated total is different than the cost of 200, that we see in the header and that is originated from the Item Master Data. SAP Business one provides an automatic routine that updates the Production Std. Cost of the item according to the calculated cost in the bill of materials. Let us see it in the next slide.

Production Std. Cost Rollup Production Production Std. Cost Management Production Std. Cost Roll Up Inventory Item Master Data Production Tab Relevant for produced items that are marked as included in the rollup procedure. In Production Production Std. Cost Management Production Std. Cost Roll Up, we can choose which items to update. Once we choose OK, the Production Std. Cost in the Item Master Data is updated according to the calculated Production Std. Cost of the Bill of Materials. Before we run the roll up procedure, we need to make sure the items are marked as Included in Production Std. Cost Rollup. Note that the roll up procedure is calculated for all levels of the Bill of Material.

Production Std. Cost Update Production Production Std. Cost Management Production Std. Cost Update Relevant for all items First perform a Production Std. Cost Update Then the Std. Cost Rollup procedure The rollup procedure updated the Production Std. Cost of produced items according to their components’ Production Std. Cost. In the Production Std. Cost Update window we can update the items’ Production Std. Cost, according to their actual cost. This procedure works similarly to the rollup procedure. In the Production Std. Cost Update window, choose the relevant items and choose the Ok button. The update is done instantly. Note that in the Selection Criteria window you can choose any item, even if it is not a produced item nor a component. In a manufacturing company, it is recommended to first perform a Production Std. Cost Update and then a rollup procedure. This way we update the actual cost of the components and then roll it up to the Production Std. Cost of the produced item. Note that this feature does not apply to non perpetual inventory managed companies.

Key Points Key points from this topic: The Production Std. Cost feature allows us to plan a budget for the production cost. The Production Std. cost can be entered manually or copied via the rollups procedure. The Production Std. Cost Rollup procedure updates the Production Std. Cost in the Item Master Data of the produced items according to the calculated Production Std. Cost in the Bill of Materials. In the Production Std. Cost Update window we can update the items’ Production Std. Cost, according to their actual cost. This feature is relevant for all items.
